keyFindings.description: claimReady takes the kept decisions (TakeParkedDecisions deletes them) and their only remaining copy is the prose in CatchUp.Decided inside one outbox row. DropCatchUps carries that text forward when a later ready drops the row, but the three undelivered branches of the notice executor (outbox.go:645 errNoticeUnroutable, :667 stoppedWithTree, :687 architectEnded) re-keep nothing, so a catch-up that finishes undelivered destroys what it took. Judged minor, not a change this round requires: every decision claimReady can take was already relayed to the controller, which holds the record and comments on the issue, except through a three-way race (a root waiting for its slot, a decision kept with no controller notice, and an architect claim that becomes ready and then fails before its catch-up row runs — the last needs an operator relaunch). Closing it properly means structuring CatchUp.Decided as rows rather than prose, which changes the agent-facing notice shape; that is the architect's call. Recorded in the pull request's Not proven / risk line.

The two relay paths disagree on one root state. workflow/parked_decision.go:39-44 suppresses the controller notice for a root that waits for its slot (waitsForSlot) and keeps the decision only; the outbox path has no such check, so a spec decision whose publish meets no holder relays to the controller for the same root. Reachable only narrowly — a re-admitted root's gate is cleared by ClearTreeGeneration, so applyArtifact has no registered gate to fire on — and harmless when it happens: the controller reads issues.<root>.phase, finds it is not done, and does nothing (skills/legion-controller/references/parked-decisions.md:41-50). Stating the rule once (a record-level helper both relays consult, as record.TreeLingers already does for the linger) is the fix if it is ever made.

Security[agent-def]: the controller decides "is this park my own hold?" from a magic comment string (`Parked by Legion while it waits on:`) posted by any session within 10 minutes of a park line authored by `session legion-daemon:<PROJECT>`. The park line's author cannot be forged (only the daemon writes it), so an attacker must wait for a daemon-written park — an operator's `legion status` among them — and post the mark inside the window to make the controller set the root to `todo`. The consequence is that the tree runs again, which is what a person does anyway, so this is hardening, not an exploit. The daemon knows the fact exactly (record.Issue.Hold, surfaced as holdReason) and could carry it on the notice; that is a design change the architect owns.

parkedDecision's {key, sent, unnamed, ref} struct and its log method exist only so the three call sites can log; all three pass the same argument list but for the row id. Giving parkDecision the row id and logging inside it would delete the struct, the method and three call-site blocks. Named as the one Fast-follow.

Validate's three ControllerNotice checks overlap: the first ((Kind == ParkedDecisionNotice) != (Decision != "")) is already covered by the second for the parked side and by the third for every other kind. Two branches state it once. Wording only; no behaviour differs.
